name: GP2Y0E03 I2C IR distance sensor
description: Sharp infrared triangulation distance sensor, 4-50 cm, with a 12-bit I2C distance output (1/64 cm steps at the default 64 cm full scale) and an analog voltage output. VDD 2.7-5.5 V; VIN(IO) sets the I2C/GPIO1 logic level and may share VDD only up to 3.3 V, so run both from 3.3 V. I2C address 0x40 (Sharp's 8-bit 0x80/0x81). GPIO1 high = measuring, low = stand-by. Sold as: Sharp GP2Y0E03 distance sensor module (bare Sharp/Socle board with 7-pin 1.25 mm JST cable: VDD, Vout(A), GND, VIN(IO), GPIO1, SCL, SDA), e.g. Robu.in / Switch Science / AliExpress listings.
eli5: Shines invisible light at an object and tells your board how far away it is, from 4 to 50 cm.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Sensor supply, 2.7-5.5 V (3.3 V here, shared with VIN(IO))

pins.name: Vout(A)
pins.description: Analog distance output, about 2.2 V at 4 cm to 0.55 V at 50 cm (nonlinear); not needed with I2C

pins.name: VIN(IO)
pins.description: I/O supply that sets the SDA/SCL/GPIO1 logic level; tie to 3.3 V (must stay below 3.6 V)

pins.name: GPIO1
pins.description: Active/stand-by input: high = measuring, low = stand-by (20 uA). Drive high from a GPIO or tie to VIN(IO)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (open drain, no pull-up on the sensor board), up to 400 kHz

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (open drain, no pull-up on the sensor board)

supplierQuery: Sharp GP2Y0E03 I2C IR distance sensor 4-50cm with cable
buildNotes: The sensor has a 7-pin 1.25 mm JST connector, not 0.1 in pins: use the matching cable and wire its leads to the header in datasheet order 1 VDD, 2 Vout(A), 3 GND, 4 VIN(IO), 5 GPIO1, 6 SCL, 7 SDA.
Feed VDD and VIN(IO) from 3.3 V. If VDD is ever run from 5 V, VIN(IO) must stay on a separate supply below 3.6 V.
GPIO1 must be high for the sensor to measure; wait at least 500 us after raising it before the first I2C access.
Read 2 bytes from register 0x5E: distance = ((b0 << 4) | (b1 & 0x0F)) / 16 / 2^n cm, where n is register 0x35 (2 by default, 64 cm full scale).
SDA and SCL are open drain with no pull-ups on the sensor: add 4.7 kOhm pull-ups to 3.3 V.
It draws 26 mA on average (36 mA max) in pulses from its IR LED; put a 10 uF capacitor across VDD/GND near the connector.
Readings beyond 50 cm are outside the specified range and are unreliable; avoid direct sunlight or lamp light on the detector.

driver.code:
# Sharp GP2Y0E03 I2C/analog IR distance sensor (4-50 cm), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the Sharp GP2Y0E02/03 application note (Table.11 register map, bank 0):
#   0x35 Shift Bit [2:0]  (0x02 = 64 cm full scale, default; 0x01 = 128 cm)
#   0x5E Distance[11:4], 0x5F Distance[3:0]
#   distance (cm) = (Distance[11:4] * 16 + Distance[3:0]) / 16 / 2**n,  n = Shift Bit
# 7-bit I2C address 0x40 (Sharp writes it as 0x80 write / 0x81 read). Max 400 kHz.
# GPIO1 must be HIGH (active state); I2C access is allowed 500 us after GPIO1 goes high.
import time
from machine import Pin

GP2Y0E03_ADDR = 0x40

_REG_SHIFT = 0x35
_REG_DIST_HI = 0x5E
_REG_BANK = 0xEF


class GP2Y0E03:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=GP2Y0E03_ADDR, gpio1=None):
        """gpio1: GPIO number wired to the sensor's GPIO1 pin (driven high = active),
        or None if GPIO1 is tied to VIN(IO) in hardware."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self._en = None
        if gpio1 is not None:
            self._en = Pin(gpio1, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        time.sleep_ms(1)  # T6/T8: >= 500 us before the first I2C access
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _REG_BANK, b'\x00')  # select register bank 0
        self.shift = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _REG_SHIFT, 1)[0] & 0x07

    def active(self, on=True):
        """Switch between active (GPIO1 high) and stand-by (GPIO1 low, about 20 uA)."""
        if self._en is None:
            raise ValueError('GPIO1 is not connected to a pin')
        self._en.value(1 if on else 0)
        if on:
            time.sleep_ms(1)

    def set_max_range(self, cm=64):
        """Full-scale output: 64 cm (Shift Bit 2, default) or 128 cm (Shift Bit 1).
        Accuracy is only specified up to 50 cm either way."""
        n = 2 if cm <= 64 else 1
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _REG_SHIFT, bytes([n]))
        self.shift = n

    def raw(self):
        """12-bit distance value from registers 0x5E (bits 11:4) and 0x5F (bits 3:0)."""
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _REG_DIST_HI, 2)
        return (d[0] << 4) | (d[1] & 0x0F)

    def distance_cm(self):
        """Distance in cm = raw / 16 / 2**shift (datasheet Table.11)."""
        return self.raw() / 16 / (1 << self.shift)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from gp2y0e03 import GP2Y0E03

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = GP2Y0E03(i2c, gpio1={GPIO1})
while True:
    print('D=%.1f cm' % sensor.distance_cm())
    time.sleep_ms(500)
